**Returns:** `{ applied: bool (THE oracle), requested: int, actually_redone: int (compare against requested), undo_count: int, can_redo: bool, next_redo: string (label of the next redoable entry) }`

## `reload_asset_package`

*Destructive.*

Re-read already-loaded packages FROM DISK, non-interactively (it never opens the modal that would freeze a headless editor), either preserving or permanently discarding their in-memory edits. This is the repair for the situation list_dirty_packages flags: a vendored package left dirty by a compile cascade is cleaned with on_dirty="discard" (was_dirty:[...] -> still_dirty:[]), so the next bulk save cannot write it. Also the way to throw away a bad in-memory edit without touching disk. It reports before/after evidence per package, and skips what it cannot safely reload (not loaded, OFPA, worlds) instead of pretending. WARNING: on_dirty="discard" is irreversible for unsaved work -- check what is dirty first.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package_names` | array | no | Array of long package names (or object paths) to reload, e.g. ["/Game/VendorPack/.../DT_ItemRows"]. |
| `package_name` | string | no | Convenience single-name alias for package_names. |
| `on_dirty` | string | no | Optional "abort" (default) or "discard". "abort" -> EReloadPackagesInteractionMode::AssumeNegative: a package with unsaved in-memory edits is NOT reloaded and its edits are kept. "discard" -> AssumePositive: UPackageTools clears the dirty flag and reloads, PERMANENTLY THROWING AWAY those in-memory edits. |

**Returns:** `{ requested: [string], on_dirty: string, interaction_mode: string, attempted: [string], reloaded: [string], was_dirty: [string], still_dirty: [string], failed: [string], skipped_not_loaded: [string], skipped_ofpa: [string], skipped_world: [object], skipped_invalid: [object], api_returned: bool, api_error: string, verify: { before: [object], after: [object] }, message: string }`

## `remove_component_from_actor`

*Destructive.*

Detach and destroy one component from an actor PLACED in the level, by component name -- the inverse of add_component_to_actor and, like it, an instance-level edit that does not touch the actor's Blueprint (use remove_component_from_blueprint for the class). Discover the exact component_name with get_actor_components first. Editor world only; dirties the actor's package, so save_level to keep it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Name of the placed actor (editor world). |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Exact component name as reported by get_actor_components. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name: string, removed_component: string, component_type: string, success: bool }`

## `remove_enum_entry`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove one enumerator from a Blueprint Enum by display name (or internal name).  Idempotent (a missing entry reports already_absent without error); refuses to remove the last remaining entry. The hidden _MAX sentinel is never counted or removable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enum_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UUserDefinedEnum. |
| `entry_name` | string | yes | Enumerator to remove, by display name (or internal name). |

**Returns:** `{ enum_path: string, entry_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, entry_count: int }`

## `remove_struct_member`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove one member from a Blueprint user-defined struct, found by display name or else by internal var name (case-insensitive), through the engine's struct editor: one undo step, the struct is recompiled so the Blueprints and DataTable rows that use it lose that field, and the package is marked dirty but not saved (save_asset). Idempotent: a member that is not there changes nothing and answers already_absent true. Removing the last member is refused, since a struct cannot be empty, and nothing changes; a path that does not load as a user-defined struct is an error. Find the names with get_struct_members; inverse: add_struct_member; to keep the data under another name use rename_struct_member instead.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `struct_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the user-defined struct, e.g. "/Game/Data/S_Item", as get_struct_members takes it. |
| `member_name` | string | yes | Member to remove, by its display name as get_struct_members returns it (members[].name) or by its var_name; case-insensitive. |

**Returns:** `{ struct_path: string, member_name: string, removed: bool, already_absent: bool, member_count: int }`

## `remove_undo_barrier`

*Destructive.*

Lift the most recent undo barrier so undo can step past it again -- the counterpart of set_undo_barrier, for when the protected batch is finished -- or, with all=true, every barrier at once (including ones another session or the human placed to protect their work). Nothing is undone; it only lifts the floor. WARNING: `success` is hardcoded true: `removed` is the oracle and comes back false as an honest no-op when there was no barrier.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `all` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false). true clears ALL undo barriers instead of popping the most recent one. |

**Returns:** `{ success: bool (hardcoded), removed: bool (THE oracle -- false = there was nothing to pop), all: bool (echo), undo_barrier: int now in force, undo_count: int, queue_length: int }`

## `rename_enum_entry`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Rename one enumerator of a Blueprint Enum (UUserDefinedEnum): resolve the entry by its current display name (or internal name) to its index, then set a new display name via FEnumEditorUtils::SetEnumeratorDisplayName.  Idempotent: renaming an entry to the name it already has is a no-op success (already_named). An unknown current entry is an honest error; so is a new name that is empty/invalid or duplicates another entry's display name (the engine's IsEnumeratorDisplayNameValid rejects it). The hidden _MAX sentinel is never addressable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enum_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UUserDefinedEnum (e.g. /Game/Blueprints/MyEnum). |
| `entry_name` | string | yes | Enumerator to rename, by its current display name (or internal name). |
| `new_name` | string | yes | New display name for the enumerator. |

**Returns:** `{ enum_path: string, entry_name: string, new_name: string, renamed: bool, already_named: bool, index: int, entries: [string] }`

## `rename_struct_member`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Rename a member of a user-defined struct by resolving its current display name to its stable VarGuid, then applying the new display name (the same FStructureEditorUtils::RenameVariable path add_struct_member uses to set the initial name).  Idempotent: renaming a member to the name it already has is a no-op success (already_named). An unknown current member, or a new name that collides with another member's name, is an honest error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `struct_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UUserDefinedStruct. |
| `member_name` | string | yes | Member to rename, by its current display name (or internal var name). |
| `new_name` | string | yes | New display name for the member. |

**Returns:** `{ struct_path: string, member_name: string, new_name: string, renamed: bool, already_named: bool, member: object }`

## `reorder_enum_entry`

*Destructive.*

Move one enumerator to a new position in a Blueprint Enum, shifting the others (e.g. [A,B,C,D] move B->index 2 = [A,C,B,D]).  to_index is clamped to the user-entry range (the trailing _MAX sentinel is excluded). An unknown entry is an honest error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enum_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UUserDefinedEnum. |
| `entry_name` | string | yes | Enumerator to move, by display name (or internal name). |
| `to_index` | number | yes | Target zero-based position among the user entries. |

**Returns:** `{ enum_path: string, entry_name: string, from_index: int, to_index: int, moved: bool, entries: [string] }`

## `reset_transaction_buffer`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

IRREVERSIBLE: wipes the editor's ENTIRE undo AND redo history (the human's entries too, not just yours) and drops any open transaction. It does not revert anything -- edits already made stay made, they just stop being undoable. Use only to reclaim memory after a huge batch, or when a corrupt buffer is causing trouble; to undo work use undo (with `count` for several steps). undo_count_before vs after is the evidence.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reason` | string | no | Human-readable reason, logged by the engine so the wipe is traceable. Defaults to 'MCP reset_transaction_buffer'. |

**Returns:** `{ success: bool (hardcoded), undo_count_before: int, undo_count_after: int (0) }`

## `run_automation_test`

*Destructive.*

Run ONE registered automation test in this editor, synchronously, and return its verdict (pass, fail or skipped) with its errors, warnings and log entries. Find the name first with list_automation_tests; re-read the last result later without running anything with get_automation_test_results; run every smoke test at once with run_smoke_tests. A test that needs several ticks (PIE, a map load, a wait) cannot be run here: it is answered verdict skipped with the reason, and no tool runs it for you -- run_functional_test_in_pie does not start a test, it only reads the verdict a Functional Test actor reports in a session where something else ran it. The same skipped answer comes for a test that needs an interactive user or a real renderer in a headless editor; an editor busy with a slow task or PIE refuses the start. Marked destructive and not idempotent because the test's own code runs in the editor and can create, change or delete assets and actors as it was written to, so two runs need not do the same; this tool itself saves nothing and adds no undo step for what the test did.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_name` | string | yes | The test's test_name or its full_test_path, exactly as list_automation_tests gives them (e.g. "UEAgent.ClaudeCode") |

**Returns:** `{ test_name, started, completed, passed, verdict, duration_s, errors, warnings, entries:[{type,message,context,filename,line}], entry_count, note }`

## `run_functional_test_in_pie`

*Destructive.*

Place one instance of a Functional Test Blueprint class in the editor level (unless one is already there) and, when no Play-in-Editor session is running or starting, request a Simulate-in-Editor session. It does not run the test (the engine's functional testing manager does, in a Play session with a player) and cannot wait for it: verdict comes from the test actor's own Result, read in the running session's world -- pass, fail, running, not_run (it has not run) or unknown (it finished with Default) -- and is not_run when no session was running at the call, since the requested one starts only after the reply (pie_requested true, pie_started usually false). With auto_stop_pie (default) the session this call requests is ended as soon as it has started; with false it keeps running until stop_play_in_editor. A session that was already running or starting is never ended. Call it again while a session runs to read the test's state; confirm the session with is_play_in_editor_active. The placed actor stays in the level, unsaved and with no undo step. Create the test first with create_functional_test; a class that is not found, is not a Functional Test, or whose name matches several loaded classes is an error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_asset_path` | string | yes | Functional Test Blueprint, as an asset path ("/Game/Tests/BP_FT_PlayerHealth", as create_functional_test returns it), object path or generated-class path ("/Game/Tests/BP_FT_PlayerHealth.BP_FT_PlayerHealth_C"); when none loads, a loaded Functional Test class named exactly like the last path segment (with or without _C) is used. |
| `auto_stop_pie` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true): end the Simulate session this call requests as soon as it has started; false leaves it running. A session that was already running is never ended. |

**Returns:** `{ test_asset_path, test_class, verdict: "pass"|"fail"|"running"|"not_run"|"unknown", test_result?, test_in_session, already_in_pie, pie_requested, pie_started, pie_stop_scheduled, spawned, already_in_world, note }`

## `run_smoke_tests`

*Destructive.*

Runs every registered automation test with the smoke filter, synchronously in the editor, and returns only the aggregate: ran, all_passed and a note. Under a commandlet the engine skips them, so ran and all_passed come back false. For one test with its log entries use run_automation_test.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ ran, all_passed, note }`

## `save_asset`

*Destructive.*

**Core tool:** every client lists it by default.

Write ONE asset's package to disk by its path (a Blueprint, DataTable, material...) and VERIFY the effect: still_dirty_after_save:false plus file_on_disk:true is the oracle, not `saved`.

Use it after an edit you want to keep: most edit tools change the asset in memory only. save_level writes a level's .umap, and reload_asset_package throws an unsaved edit away instead. Refused while Play-in-Editor runs, because the engine would drop the write and still report success (see force).

When it fails with PIE down, `file_read_only` says whether the file is read-only on disk -- a Git LFS `lockable` file that nobody has `git lfs lock`ed is the usual case -- and the error says whether that is the cause. It writes exactly one package, so it cannot stop a compile from dirtying a vendored asset that a LATER bulk save rewrites: list_dirty_packages before, `git status` after.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Full asset path to save, e.g. /Game/MyGame/Core/BP_MyActor (an .Object suffix is tolerated). Must already exist or the call errors. |
| `readonly_roots` | array | no | Optional array of long-path prefixes treated as vendored/upstream (default: the project's Read Only Content Roots). A save under one of them is REFUSED by default; see refuse_readonly. Pass [] to disable the classification entirely. |
| `refuse_readonly` | boolean | no | Optional bool. When true, a save whose package falls under one of readonly_roots is REFUSED (success:false, saved:false, refused_readonly:true) instead of performed. Default = the process-wide switch (mcp_common::IsReadOnlyRootSaveEnforcementEnabled(), true unless `mcp.ReadOnlyRootEnforcement 0`); when false the write happens and is only reported + ledgered. |

**Returns:** `` { path: string, package_name: string, saved: bool, success: bool, under_readonly_root: bool, readonly_root_matched: string, refused_readonly: bool, readonly_roots: [string], readonly_roots_defaulted: bool, still_dirty_after_save: bool, file_on_disk: bool, file_read_only: bool (measured on disk -- true means the file is read-only, e.g. an unlocked Git LFS `lockable` file), verification: object, verification_checks: [object], error?: string } ``

## `save_level`

*Destructive.*

**Pack `levels`:** `enable_toolset` adds it to a client's list ([tool lists](../clients.md#tool-lists)).

Write the editor's current level (.umap) to disk; it REFUSES while PIE is running (the engine guard rejects the write anyway) and derives `success` from the file being on disk afterwards, never from the save call's own bool. WARNING: it also REFUSES when the target .umap is READ-ONLY on disk, which in an LFS repo means a `lockable` path you have not `git lfs lock`ed: that write cannot succeed, and answering over HEAD's still-untouched bytes would report success:true having written nothing. The refusal names the file and the fix (`git lfs lock <file>`) -- take the lock, do not retry. WARNING: on a file that ALREADY existed, `file_exists_on_disk` alone still cannot tell "I wrote it" from "it was already there": the field that proves the write is `file_mtime_changed`. It is deliberately NOT gating `success`, because a save with nothing dirty to write also leaves the mtime alone and that is not a failure. WARNING: with `filename` this is a SaveAs that DUPLICATES: the editor stays on the old map, the new one becomes a resident world (which then makes load_level refuse), and a SECOND save to the same filename opens a modal that freezes the editor -- treat filename as one-shot per name per session.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `filename` | string | no | Optional. A /Game asset path (e.g. /Game/Maps/Foo) or a disk .umap path; both accepted and resolved. Omit it to save the level in place -- that is the branch that just works. Passing one is a SaveAs: duplicate + resident world + the one-shot rule above. |
| `save_as` | string | no | Accepted for wire compatibility and IGNORED: the branch is chosen by whether `filename` was given. It comes back inside `requested` to mark it as your input, not a measurement. |

**Returns:** `{ success: bool, error?: string, data?: { saved_filename?: string, saved_package?: string, saved_disk_path?: string, level_name?: string, file_exists_on_disk: bool, file_size_bytes: int, file_existed_before: bool, file_mtime_changed: bool (the write itself -- see the read-only note above), save_call_returned: bool, rescued_with_save_packages: bool, pie_was_stopped: bool, orphan_world_risk?: bool, requested?: { filename?: string, save_as?: bool } } }`

## `select_actors`

*Destructive.*

Select actors by name in the editor viewport/outliner, appending to or replacing the current selection, and report which ones were not found. Use it to stage the input for the selection-driven tools (copy_actors with copy_selected, move_actors_to_level) or to show the user what you mean before they look. WARNING: matches INTERNAL names only (no editor labels) and misses are reported in not_found_names instead of failing, so check not_found_count. Editor world only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_names` | array | yes | Array of internal actor names (GetName), case-insensitive whole-string. Editor labels do NOT resolve here; convert them with find_actors_by_name. |
| `add_to_selection` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default TRUE = append to whatever is already selected). Pass false to clear the selection first and end up with exactly these actors. |

**Returns:** `{ selected_actors: [actor JSON], selected_count: int, not_found_count: int, not_found_names?: [string], add_to_selection: bool }`

## `set_actor_transform`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Move, rotate and/or scale ONE actor (omitted components are left as they are) and return the actor's re-read transform plus the identity of the world that was written. Undoable, and it calls Modify() first -- which matters, because moving an actor from Python does NOT dirty its OFPA package and then save_level reports success while writing nothing. Takes a `world` selector, so it also reaches a LIVE PIE pawn (an editor-only lookup would answer "Actor not found" for an actor that exists in another world). Use execute_batch for many actors, snap_actor_to_landscape to drop one onto the landscape.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Actor's internal name (GetName) or editor label (GetActorLabel), case-insensitive whole-string match. |
| `world` | string | no | Optional: "editor" (default) \| "pie" \| "server" \| "client" \| "pie:N". In co-op the authoritative pawn lives on the server, and a move written to the client world will be corrected by replication. |
| `location` | array | no | Optional new WORLD location, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]. Absolute, not a delta; any other value (an object, another length) is an error and the actor is not touched. |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional new WORLD rotation as the array [pitch, yaw, roll] -- note index 2 is ROLL, not yaw -- or, unambiguously, the object {"pitch":..,"yaw":..,"roll":..}, which is the recommended form. |
| `scale` | array | no | Optional new WORLD scale, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]. Any other value (an object, another length) is an error and the actor is not touched. |

**Returns:** `{ actor JSON via DescribeActorObject, transform RE-READ off the actor after the write }`

## `set_current_level`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Choose which sub-level of the editor world is CURRENT, i.e. where newly spawned or pasted actors will land. Set it before spawn_actor / paste_actors when a map is split into streaming sub-levels, otherwise everything piles into whichever level happens to be active. Errors honestly if the named streaming level is not loaded/visible; already_current:true when it was already the one. Use move_actors_to_level to relocate actors that ended up in the wrong one.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `level_name` | string | yes | "persistent" for the persistent level, or the SHORT name of a loaded, visible streaming sub-level (not a /Game path). |

**Returns:** `{ current_level: string, changed: bool, already_current: bool, success: true } -- current_level is the level current after the call; a level that is not found, or not loaded and visible, is an error instead.`

## `set_cvar`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Sets a console variable via IConsoleManager and reads the value back.  Uses IConsoleManager::Get().FindConsoleVariable(name)->Set(value, ECVF_SetByConsole). Honest error if the named cvar does not exist (unlike a raw console Exec which silently no-ops).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Console variable name, e.g. "r.ScreenPercentage", "r.Shadow.MaxResolution". |
| `value` | any | yes | New value (string, number, or bool; coerced to the cvar's type). |

**Returns:** `{ set: bool, requested_value: string, name: string, value: string, string_value: string, int_value: int, float_value: float, bool_value: bool, help: string, flags: int, set_by: string }`

## `set_cvars_from_json`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set several console variables of the running editor in one call, from a JSON object of name/value pairs, each through IConsoleManager at SetByCode priority, then read each one back. Not atomic: names are applied one by one, and the others still apply when one fails. applied counts only the variables that hold the new value afterwards; results gives each one's read-back value and set_by. A variable last set at a higher priority (by the console or by set_cvar) ignores this write and goes to errors, as do an unknown name and a value the variable would misread; then success is false (use set_cvar, console priority, for those). Find names with list_cvars. The values live in this editor session only: nothing is written to an INI (set_engine_ini_value does that) and nothing is undoable. Text that is not a JSON object is an error and nothing changes. Repeating the call sets the same values again.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cvars` | string | yes | A STRING holding a JSON object of exact cvar names to values, e.g. '{"r.ScreenPercentage":"75","t.MaxFPS":60}'; names as list_cvars returns them. A value is text, a number (passed as its text) or a bool (passed as 1/0); a numeric or bool cvar takes only a number or one of the words true/false/yes/no/on/off (as 1/0), and other text, null, an array or an object is refused for that name. |

**Returns:** `{ applied, requested, results: [{name, requested_value, value, set_by, applied}], errors: [{name, error}] }`

## `set_engine_ini_value`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Write one key into the GConfig copy of an INI (Engine by default), flush it to the saved config under Saved/Config/&lt;Platform>/, and verify by reading it back (applied). It does not edit Config/Default*.ini, and objects that already loaded their config are not reloaded. The value may be text, a bool or a number; with plugin_name it writes a plugin's setting, the section defaulting to the plugin's /Script/&lt;Plugin>.&lt;Plugin>.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes | Key inside the section, e.g. "r.DefaultFeature.AntiAliasing"; its current value is replaced. |
| `value` | any | yes | Value to write: a string written verbatim (an empty string is allowed), a JSON bool written as GConfig writes one ("True"/"False"), or a JSON number written as its text (an integer without decimals). |
| `section` | string | no | INI section, e.g. "/Script/Engine.RendererSettings"; created when missing; surrounding brackets are dropped. Required unless plugin_name is given. |
| `config_file` | string | no | Config base name without extension, e.g. "Engine" (default), "Game", "Input"; "Engine.ini" is not resolved. |
| `plugin_name` | string | no | Optional plugin, as its .uplugin is named: an unknown one fails with nothing written; a known one adds its identity to the reply and makes section default to /Script/&lt;Plugin>.&lt;Plugin>. |

**Returns:** `{ applied, section, key, value, value_type: "string"|"bool"|"number", readback_value, config_file, config_file_path, plugin_name?, plugin_status?, plugin_version?, plugin_description?, plugin_author?, plugin_category?, plugin_loaded?, plugin_enabled?, plugin_path?, plugin_file? }`

## `set_enum_bitflags`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Turn the "Bitflags" metadata of a Blueprint Enum (UUserDefinedEnum) on or off, as the enum editor's checkbox does: on, its enumerators can be combined as bit flags, so an integer variable marked Bitmask can use it as its Bitmask Enum. Only this flag changes; build the entries with create_enum, add_enum_entry, rename_enum_entry, reorder_enum_entry or remove_enum_entry, and read them with get_enum_info. One undo step; Blueprints that use the enum are notified, and the enum is marked dirty, not saved (save_asset). Idempotent: the state it already has reports already_set=true, applied=false, and changes nothing. A path that does not load a UUserDefinedEnum (a native C++ enum included) is an error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enum_path` | string | yes | Full asset path of the UUserDefinedEnum (e.g. /Game/Blueprints/MyEnum, the ".MyEnum" suffix optional), as create_enum returns it or find_assets_by_name finds it. |
| `bitflags` | boolean | yes | Desired state: true to mark as bitflags, false to clear. |

**Returns:** `{ enum_path: string, bitflags: bool, already_set: bool, applied: bool }`

## `set_plugin_enabled`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Turn a plugin on (or off, with enabled=false) in the .uproject and save the project file to disk. WARNING: `enabled` echoes the requested state once the .uproject write succeeded, and the plugin's MODULES are not loaded or unloaded by this call -- the editor has to be restarted before an enabled plugin's classes, assets or MCP tools actually exist, and a disabled plugin's classes keep working until then. So do not treat a following "class not found", or a still-working feature, as a failure of this command; check project_saved and then restart. A plugin the .uproject already has in that state is a no-op: project_saved=false and nothing saved; a .uproject that cannot be saved makes success false. A name this editor has not discovered as a plugin is an error, and nothing is written to the .uproject. WARNING: disabling a plugin whose assets are referenced leaves those references broken on the next start; check get_plugin_status and the referencers first. Use get_plugin_status to read the current state.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plugin_name` | string | yes | Plugin name exactly as in its .uplugin file (e.g. 'PythonScriptPlugin'), not a path. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default true): true enables the plugin, false disables it. |

**Returns:** `{ plugin_name: string (the plugin's own spelling), enabled: bool (the requested state, set when the .uproject write succeeded), project_saved: bool, note: string about the required restart, or that nothing changed }`

## `set_scalability_quality`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the running editor's scalability quality, every sg.* group at once (category all, the default) or one group, through Scalability::SetQualityLevels + ApplyCachedQualityLevels, then read all the levels back. It starts from the current levels, so a single-group change leaves the other groups as they were. The change lives in this editor session only: it is not undoable and is not written to GameUserSettings, an INI or a device profile. Check the levels before with get_scalability_levels; for one sg.* or r.* variable use set_cvar instead. An unknown quality word or category is an error and nothing changes; a number outside 0-4 is clamped. The levels are read back after the change: set is true only when every group asked for now holds its level, and otherwise success is false, with mismatches naming each group the engine left elsewhere. Repeating the call sets the same levels again (idempotent).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quality` | any | no | Level as a number 0-4 (0 Low, 1 Medium, 2 High, 3 Epic, 4 Cinematic; others clamped) or one of "Low", "Medium", "High", "Epic", "Cinematic", case ignored. Required. |
| `category` | string | no | One group, case ignored: "ViewDistance", "AntiAliasing", "Shadows", "GlobalIllumination" (or "GI"), "Reflection", "PostProcess", "Texture", "Effects", "Foliage", "Shading", "Landscape"; or "all" (the default) for every group. |

**Returns:** `{ set: bool, requested_level: int, category: string, ResolutionQuality: int, ViewDistanceQuality: int, AntiAliasingQuality: int, ShadowQuality: int, GlobalIlluminationQuality: int, ReflectionQuality: int, PostProcessQuality: int, TextureQuality: int, EffectsQuality: int, FoliageQuality: int, ShadingQuality: int, LandscapeQuality: int, mismatches?: [string] }`

## `set_struct_member_default`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the default value of one member of a Blueprint user-defined struct, found by display name or else by internal var name (case-insensitive), through the engine's struct editor, which checks the value against the member's type and recompiles the struct; one undo step, and the package is marked dirty but not saved (save_asset). Idempotent: a value equal to the stored default text changes nothing and answers already_set true (compared as text, so "1.5" and "1.50" differ). A value invalid for the type, a member that is not found or a path that does not load as a user-defined struct is an error and nothing changes. Read the members and their current defaults with get_struct_members; a new member gets its type from add_struct_member first.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `struct_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the user-defined struct, e.g. "/Game/Data/S_Item", as get_struct_members takes it. |
| `member_name` | string | yes | Member to edit, by its display name as get_struct_members returns it (members[].name) or by its var_name; case-insensitive. |
| `default_value` | string | yes | New default as text in the member type's format (e.g. "7", "true", "1.5", "Hello", "(X=1.0,Y=2.0,Z=3.0)" for a Vector); pass "" to clear it. |

**Returns:** `{ struct_path: string, member_name: string, default_value: string, applied_default_value: string, already_set: bool, applied: bool, member: object }`

## `set_undo_barrier`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Drop a floor in the undo stack at the current position so no later undo can cross it -- the way to protect everything done SO FAR (yours or the human's) before starting a risky batch that you may want to unwind. Idempotent: a barrier already sitting at the cursor is not pushed twice (already_existed:true). Lift it with remove_undo_barrier (all=true lifts every barrier).

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ success: bool (hardcoded), already_existed: bool (true = nothing new was pushed), undo_barrier: int (cursor it sits at), undo_count: int, queue_length: int }`

## `set_viewport_settings`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Change any settings of the active level editor viewport (the focused one, else the first) in one call: camera location and rotation, field of view, near and far clip planes, exposure, realtime, view mode, show flags, camera speed, perspective or orthographic view type, game view and cinematic control. Pass only the settings to change; each is validated and applied as its own step, in the order listed here, and the call stops at the first one refused (applied lists those already changed). Editor view only: not undoable, nothing saved. get_viewport_state reads every one of them back.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `location` | string | no | Optional camera [x, y, z] world location |
| `rotation` | string | no | Optional camera world rotation, [pitch, yaw, roll] or {"pitch","yaw","roll"} |
| `fov` | number | no | Optional perspective field of view in degrees |
| `near_clip` | number | no | Optional near clip plane distance in cm |
| `far_clip` | number | no | Optional far clip plane distance in cm; 0 means no far plane |
| `exposure_fixed` | boolean | no | Optional: true for a fixed exposure at exposure_ev100, false for automatic eye adaptation |
| `exposure_ev100` | number | no | Optional EV100 used when exposure_fixed is true (typical range -3..20); needs exposure_fixed |
| `realtime` | boolean | no | Optional: realtime rendering on or off |
| `view_mode` | string | no | Optional engine view mode name, e.g. Lit, Unlit, Wireframe, DetailLighting, LightingOnly, ShaderComplexity, Clay |
| `show_flags` | object | no | Optional {flag_name: bool} of engine show flags (Grid, Bounds, Collision, Fog...) set to that state |
| `camera_speed` | number | no | Optional camera movement speed, above 0 |
| `view_type` | string | no | Optional: Perspective, Top, Bottom, Left, Right, Front or Back |
| `game_view` | boolean | no | Optional: game view on (editor-only icons and gizmos hidden) or off |
| `allow_cinematic_control` | boolean | no | Optional: whether Sequencer may drive this viewport's camera |

**Returns:** `{ applied: { setting: that setting's reply }, failed?: { label, command, error } (when a setting is refused) }`

## `show_notification`

*Additive.*

Show a transient toast in the editor through the Slate notification manager: message, an optional completion state icon and a lifetime in seconds, after which it fades on its own. completion_state is matched without case, and anything other than Pending, Success or Fail shows no state; the reply echoes it as sent, not as applied. Each call shows another toast, so it is not idempotent, and nothing else changes: no asset, log line or undo step. shown is false when the notification manager returned no toast, and the call still succeeds. An empty or missing message is an error. For a record that stays use print_to_output_log or add_message_log_entry.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | yes | The text to display in the notification; empty is an error. |
| `completion_state` | string | no | Completion state, case-insensitive: "None" (default), "Pending", "Success" or "Fail"; any other value counts as "None". |
| `duration` | number | no | Notification lifetime in seconds before it fades (default 4.0); the value is not validated. |

**Returns:** `{ shown: bool, message: string, completion_state: string, duration: float }`

## `snap_actor_to_ground`

*Destructive.*

Drop ONE editor-world actor straight down until its bounds bottom rests on whatever is below -- meshes, BSP or the landscape. It line-traces first and, because headless traces routinely MISS the landscape, falls back to sampling the heightmap so the actor still lands; sampled_from tells you which path answered. Use snap_actor_to_landscape when the ground is definitely the landscape and you want no trace at all, execute_batch for many actors.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Name of the actor to snap (editor world). |
| `trace_distance` | number | no | Optional downward trace distance in cm; defaults to 10000 |
| `align_to_surface` | boolean | no | When true, rotate actor to match the surface normal (trace hits only; the heightmap fallback has no normal); defaults to false |
| `fallback_heightmap` | boolean | no | When true (default) and the downward line trace misses (headless traces routinely miss the landscape), fall back to sampling the landscape heightmap at the actor's XY (same sampler as snap_actor_to_landscape) so the actor still lands. Set false to require a real trace hit. |

**Returns:** `{ actor: actor JSON, hit: bool, landed: bool, sampled_from: 'trace'|'heightmap', hit_actor?: string, hit_distance?: number }`

## `snap_actor_to_landscape`

*Destructive.*

Ground an actor on the landscape by sampling the heightmap at its XY (no line trace; traces miss the landscape headless). Sets the actor's Z so either its mesh bbox bottom or its origin sits at the sampled height + z_offset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Internal name of the actor to place (Actor->GetName()) |
| `align` | string | no | Optional 'mesh_bbox_bottom' (default; drops the lowest mesh-geometry point onto the ground) or 'actor_origin' (puts the actor origin at the ground) |
| `z_offset` | number | no | Optional extra world-Z added above the sampled ground height; defaults to 0 |

**Returns:** `{ actor: actor JSON, landed_z: number (sampled ground world-Z), previous_z: number, new_z: number, sampled_from: 'heightmap', in_bounds: bool, align: string, align_used: string, z_offset: number, landscape_actor_name: string }`

## `spawn_actor`

*Destructive.*

**Pack `actors`:** `enable_toolset` adds it to a client's list ([tool lists](../clients.md#tool-lists)).

Place an actor of ANY placeable class -- a built-in short name (StaticMeshActor, PointLight, SpotLight, DirectionalLight, RectLight, SkyLight, CameraActor, Character), another engine or plugin class by name or path (SkyAtmosphere, ExponentialHeightFog, VolumetricCloud, SceneCapture2D, TextRenderActor, NiagaraActor, /Script/Engine.DecalActor...) or a Blueprint asset path -- into the editor level or a live PIE world, at an optional location/rotation/scale, and set its properties in the same call: properties={"Prop": v} on the actor, {"Component.Prop": v} on a component named so or of a class only one component has (e.g. {"ExponentialHeightFogComponent.FogDensity": 0.05}), written as set_properties writes them. A volume needs a brush: spawn_box_volume places one; an abstract or non-placeable class is refused. Refuses a name an actor already has (omit name to let the engine pick a unique one); the spawn is undoable. A property that cannot be written makes the call fail with properties_failed while the actor stays, so fix it with set_properties or remove it with delete_actor. It creates the actor in MEMORY only -- save_level (with the .umap writable) puts it on disk. WARNING: with 2+ PIE clients world='pie' can land in the CLIENT world, producing an actor the authority never sees -- ask for world='server' instead, and check has_authority and world_package in the reply.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | yes | The actor class: a built-in short name (StaticMeshActor, PointLight, SpotLight, DirectionalLight, RectLight, SkyLight, CameraActor, Character; a light also as Point, Spot, Directional, Rect or Sky), any other actor class by name or /Script path, or a Blueprint asset path (/Game/BP_Door). Volumes go through spawn_box_volume. |
| `name` | string | no | Optional internal name (and label) for the new actor; must be unused in the target world or the call is refused. When omitted the engine names the actor uniquely and the label is the class default. |
| `location` | array | no | Optional world location, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]; the origin when omitted. Any other value (an object, another length) is an error and nothing is spawned. |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional world rotation as the array [pitch, yaw, roll] -- note index 2 is ROLL, not yaw -- or, unambiguously, the object {"pitch":..,"yaw":..,"roll":..}, which is the recommended form. Defaults to zero. Directional, spot and rect lights shine along its forward axis. |
| `scale` | array | no | Optional world scale, ARRAY form only: [x, y, z]. Defaults to 1,1,1; any other value (an object, another length) is an error and nothing is spawned. |
| `static_mesh` | string | no | Optional UStaticMesh asset path, only honoured for type=StaticMeshActor (e.g. /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube). |
| `intensity` | number | no | Optional, light types only: the light component's Intensity in the light's units (Directional: lux; Sky: a multiplier); engine default when omitted. Sent for a non-light type it is refused and nothing is spawned. |
| `color` | array | no | Optional, light types only: [r, g, b] linear color, usually 0..1; engine default (white) when omitted. Sent for a non-light type it is refused and nothing is spawned. |
| `properties` | object | no | Optional {"Prop": value, "Component.Prop": value} written after the spawn with set_properties' writer: engine property names, a struct as a JSON object of the fields to change. |
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector for WHERE the actor is spawned: absent/'editor' (default) \| 'pie' (ambiguous: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'game' (alias of 'pie') \| 'server' (the PIE world with authority -- what you want for anything replicated) \| 'client' \| 'pie:N'. Case-insensitive; an unrecognised value is a clean error listing the worlds present, never a silent spawn into the editor world. |

**Returns:** `{ actor JSON via DescribeActorObject: name, class, location, rotation, scale, plus world: string (the normalized selector that resolved), world_name: string, world_package: string (the UEDPIE_N prefix lives HERE), world_type: string, net_mode: string, pie_instance: int, has_authority: bool, local_role: string, light_intensity?: number (light types: the intensity now on the component), light_color?: [r, g, b] (light types: the color now on the component), properties_set?: [string], properties_failed?: [{property, error}] (with properties) }`

## `undo`

*Destructive.*

**Core tool:** every client lists it by default.

Step the editor's undo stack back by one transaction, or by `count` of them, as Ctrl+Z does, and report what is now on top (next_undo, the label of the next entry).

Use it to revert an edit made in the editor, by a tool or by the person at the keyboard: the stack is shared, so the newest entry may be theirs -- read get_undo_state first to see the label you are about to revert. One transaction is usually one tool call that changed something; to make several edits one entry, wrap them in begin_transaction and end_transaction. Undo reverts objects in memory, not files: an edit saved since stays in the file on disk until the next save.

WARNING: `success` is ALWAYS true, including when there was nothing to undo -- the oracle is `applied`, and with a count compare actually_undone against requested (the stack ran out, or an undo barrier stopped it); the honest verification is re-reading whatever you changed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | number | no | Optional. How many transactions to undo, at least 1 (default 1); stops early when the stack runs out or reaches an undo barrier. Below 1 is refused. |

**Returns:** `{ applied: bool, requested: int, actually_undone: int, undo_count: int, can_undo: bool, next_undo: string }`
